pr_body:
This PR introduces these two changes:

1. If Node reports a client timeout (`ERR_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`) it returns a HTTP 408 in clientError handling rather than 400.
2. The fastify object now supports the `http` option that, similarly to `https` is directly forwarded to Node's HTTP server.

Fixes #4535.

#### Checklist

- [x] run `npm run test` and `npm run benchmark`
- [x] tests and/or benchmarks are included
- [x] documentation is changed or added
- [x] commit message and code follows the [Developer's Certification of Origin](https://github.com/fastify/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#developers-certificate-of-origin-11)
      and the [Code of conduct](https://github.com/fastify/.github/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

comments: Thanks for reporting! Would you like to send a Pull Request to address this issue? Remember to add unit tests.

> So there seems to be bigger issue under the hood?

It depends on how fast to receive the request. 
If you want a reliable one, I suggest to use `POST` with large payload.
